answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in earned history instead of cheap creation: every new agent starts at the tide line with zero reputation and must collect attestations from established peers by doing verifiable work, each attestation recorded in a shared kernel ledger. Reaching the zenith of full earning rights takes weeks of consistent, checked output, so an attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities gains nothing — each one must pay the same slow time-and-work cost, while a single honest agent's record compounds.
